name: Koch Curve
miniText: How can a finite replacement rule create an increasingly intricate curve? NetLogo Koch Curve repeatedly replaces each segment with four shorter segments arranged around a triangular bump. The construction makes successive approximations visible, allowing segment count, scale, and apparent roughness to be compared. Chaos and Fractals [1] explains self-similar constructions and dimension; Mandelbrot's research monograph [2] places such curves within fractal geometry; the Algorithmic Beauty of Plants [3] provides a complementary rewriting and turtle-graphics formulation. The mathematical limiting curve differs fundamentally from any finite display: the simulation always stops at a finite iteration depth and finite numerical resolution. The model illustrates recursive substitution and scaling, rather than directly simulating erosion or coastline formation. Similar-looking natural boundaries require their own mechanisms and empirical measurements before fractal analogies become explanatory claims.
